correctness.rationale: The proof fixes the unnormalized Walsh convention, uses the weighted matrix-tree theorem with negative weights, and reconstructs the coefficient-of-t identity even with extra zero eigenvalues. Symmetric/antisymmetric rail diagonalization yields the explicit half-determinant. Odd length: the classical tau_n recurrence makes all Walsh coefficients odd and the all-negative-rungs coefficient is +/-1 by an exact path spectrum identity. Even length: the explicit period-four vector gives an eigenvalue 2 for every prescribed independent even-edge sign choice, producing \(2^{n/2-1}\) distinct zeros. Fourier diagonalization then yields exact \(\ell^2\) operator and inverse norms. Standard-library standalone checker independently enumerates all frequencies to n=7, exact determinant to n=13, and witness families through n=22. Finite checks are corroboration, not universal proofs.

value.rationale: The object is the canonical spanning-tree indicator of an open grid strip on a Boolean edge cube. Its Fourier zero set controls whether a natural finite-group convolution is invertible. The theorem gives a complete infinite-width invertibility classification, the exact sharp minimum eigenvalue and \(\ell^2\) spectral condition number in every invertible case, and an exponential explicit family of null frequencies otherwise. The result distinguishes ordinary counting parity from a second signed-Laplacian cancellation mechanism; it is not an isolated numerical census or an arbitrary normalization test.
